canada.title: Ontario Liberals to select 3rd new leader since 2018
canada.summary: The 2023 leadership race that crowned Bonnie Crombie leader saw friction between her and runner-up Nate Erskine-Smith.

canada.title: How a small Toronto radio program is bringing Afghan women's voices to light
canada.summary: A Toronto radio program is providing the opportunity for women living under the Taliban regime to share their stories. Radio Jawan operates like a journalism school, and is run by a former reporter in Afghanistan who settled in the GTA

canada.title: Wild’s Hughes, Kaprizov chasing history in win
canada.summary: Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes accomplished a feat that's only been done once in the last 33 years.

canada.title: Hunger Games prequel satiates
canada.summary: “Nothing is inevitable,” says one of the characters in this new Hunger Games prequel.

canada.title: Woman who died kayaking near Squamish remembered by close friend
canada.summary: Family and friends are remembering a 29-year-old Squamish, B.C., woman who died while kayaking for her passion for adventure and infectious smile. Lucia Belakova died after her kayak capsized on the Cheakamus River on Nov. 15, 2026.

canada.title: What will new mandatory phys-ed courses for Alberta high school students look like?
canada.summary: Starting in 2028, students in their last two years of high school will need to take a combination physical education, wellness and financial literacy course, with one credit in each subject. But some are raising concerns about gym space and available teachers to make it happen.

canada.title: Threatening message about City of Weyburn pool project sparks calls to improve discourse
canada.summary: The now-deleted comment, which made reference to shooting city officials, is part of "a broader pattern of hostile and personally directed comments toward members of City Council and municipal employees across the country," the city said in a statement.

canada.title: Generator repairs and overhaul in Rankin Inlet, Nunavut, will mean easier winter, says Qulliq Energy
canada.summary: Last winter, the community experienced six power outages in as many weeks when two of Qulliq Energy Corporation's four main generators were out of service.

canada.title: Northern Manitoba fire chiefs look for new equipment, more volunteers following wildfires
canada.summary: After devastating forest fire seasons in 2024 and 2025, two northern Manitoba fire departments adapting to changing needs are looking for help — one with new equipment, one with finding more volunteer firefighters.

canada.title: N.B. patients face 3½-hour ER waits, down an hour from previous year, report finds
canada.summary: New Brunswick emergency room patients typically waited about 3½ hours to be either admitted to hospital or discharged in 2025-26, down an hour from the previous year, according to a new report by a public policy think-tank.

canada.title: ‘We’re at a loss’: private clinics frustrated by provincial cap on cataract surgeries
canada.summary: In 2025, New Brunswick started funding cataract surgeries in private clinics to address a significant patient backlog. But with more than four months left in the fiscal year, some clinics are already close to hitting their quotas.

canada.title: They finally had their dream food truck. Then it was repossessed
canada.summary: A family ran their business, LeoMay Fusion, out of a food truck for about a year in rural Nova Scotia until RCMP officers showed up in mid-October and they learned a previous lender was repossessing the vehicle.

canada.title: Parents say this N.S. driving school ‘ghosted’ them after they paid hundreds of dollars
canada.summary: Several parents with children enrolled in Marshall Law Driving Academy say they feel blindsided by its sudden closure last week after each paying the company hundreds of dollars.

canada.title: Pilot program that welcomes doctors in training to Yukon on path to permanency
canada.summary: Health Minister Brad Cathers says the Yukon government and University of Alberta aim to bring more family medicine residents into the territory on an ongoing basis. The pilot program has so far brought in three residents, including two Yukoners.

canada.title: Metrobus still working on staffing shortages as it gears up for recruitment push this weekend
canada.summary: Metrobus will be holding an open house on Saturday, Nov. 21 for anyone who may be interested in a position as a driver or mechanic, or in otherwise contributing to maintaining and expanding public transit.

canada.title: Housing project in Brossard, Que., promised affordability. Residents struck it down
canada.summary: The City of Brossard is asking a developer to go back to the drawing board after a group of residents blocked a housing project that would have brought 810 units, including affordable housing, to the city's edge.

canada.title: A Montrealer died in Istanbul. Authorities blame food poisoning but what we found suggests something else
canada.summary: A young Canadian woman travelled to Turkey after graduating from medical school. In her last days there, she fell ill and died within hours. Authorities there blame food poisoning, but a joint investigation by Enquête and the fifth estate revealed 12 similar deaths and a different poison at work.

canada.title: 5 Mission teens arrested after video posted online of another swarming attack
canada.summary: Police say assault charges have been recommended against all five youths -- including some who allegedly encouraged the attack rather than physically participating.

bds.h: International court's ruling on Myanmar genocide means little for victims, but much for future cases
bds.lede: Legal experts say the International Court of Justice's first ever finding of genocide committed by a state may also help shape how that case and others like it are decided in the future. Victims, human rights activists and legal observers had hoped that the case, filed against Myanmar in 2019, would open a new pathway for delivering justice on the international stage.
